_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); railroad signals

pit_profile.why: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not

classification.quality_note: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price fair; Ratio B 1.09x; +26% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.13; conservative 2yr +16%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -7.7%/yr (worst year FY15-FY24, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +8.0%/yr (Q2 2025 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +8.1%/yr (FY15-FY24 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +24.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY15-FY24); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: UNP (retrospective, 2025-08-29) ◎ ACCUMULATE — Ratio B 1.09x (27.5% downside to Bear $162 / +25.2% upside to Bull $280) | Adj composite 2.84 vs market 2.97: gap -0.13 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +26% above the EPP floor $177 (16x FY25E $11.09) | Conservative 2-yr case: +16.5% total (+8.2%/yr) | At 20.2x FY25E the 15% hurdle price $296 sits above the BULL case; carloads +4% in Q2 2025, forward revenue +4% (no FY25 revenue guide, Q2 2025 freight revenue); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation 8-K (Item 7.01): 2024 Investor Day financial guidance
sources.supports: over the next 3 years: revenue excluding fuel surcharge to grow faster than volume excluding coal, which will outpace the markets served; pricing dollars accretive to operating ratio starting in 2025; an industry leading operating ratio; an EPS compound annual growth rate in the high single to low double digit range; capital of $3.5-3.7 billion a year; $4-5 billion of annual share repurchases starting in 2025; a dividend payout target of about 45%
